sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusables and KG hints, Railroad crossings, pedestrians, school buses and bicyclists

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A01
A closed railroad gate may never be driven through, around or under, while an open crossing still requires a reduced speed and, when lights, a gate, a flagman, a train or a stop sign requires it, a stop at least fifteen feet from the nearest rail [A01].
Why it matters: group railroad crossings; difficulty medium; prereq sec07-F02; confusables sec07-F02, sec07-F04
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A04
Alternately flashing yellow lights on a school bus mean prepare to stop, while alternately flashing red lights mean you must be stopped [A04].
Why it matters: group school buses; difficulty medium; prereq sec07-F26; confusables sec07-F26, sec07-F27
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A04
The school bus stop exception covers a bus going the other way on a divided highway or behind a concrete barrier, but not a bus on an undivided road and not one inside a school yard [A04].
Why it matters: group school buses; difficulty high; prereq sec07-F27; confusables sec07-F28, sec07-F27
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A02
A pedestrian with a white cane or a guide dog requires a full stop and yield, whereas other pedestrians require yielding without necessarily a stop [A02].
Why it matters: group pedestrians; difficulty medium; prereq sec07-F10; confusables sec07-F14, sec07-F10
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A04
A driver must leave at least four feet when passing a bicyclist, which is a clearance rule, distinct from the bicyclist's own right to use the whole lane when the road is too narrow to share [A04].
Why it matters: group bicyclists; difficulty medium; prereq sec07-F30; confusables sec07-F35, sec07-F32
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A03
A pedestrian without a sidewalk walks on the left facing traffic, the opposite of a bicyclist, who rides on the right with traffic [A03].
Why it matters: group pedestrians; difficulty low; prereq sec07-F23; confusables sec07-F23, sec07-F30
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0040]
